messages:
maria: FYI escalation from an enterprise customer — they started seeing embedding vectors double in length after switching to the `-int8` variant. Their vector DB rejects writes with a schema error. Posting their minimal repro and logs below.

maria: customer curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-mini-int8","input":["doc1","doc2"]}'
```

maria: response snippet they captured:
```
{"model":"rwd-embed-mini-int8","version":"2026-03-02-qv1","embedding_dim":512,"data":[{"embedding":[0.001, -0.002, ...]}]}
```

maria: Their app previously consumed 256-dimensional vectors from `rwd-embed-mini-fp16` and everything worked. They rolled back client code and still get 512. Customer is asking if quantization changed dimensions.

devon: quick answer: quantization (fp16/int8) by itself does NOT change the embedding dimension. Precision changes numeric representation, not the projection size. Doubling typically means a different head/projection or multi-pooling (e.g., concatenating mean+cls). Could be aliasing in model registry where `-int8` mapped to a different checkpoint.

devon: can you ask for the raw `model`/`version` JSON and whether their SDK logged any alternate model name during the bulk ingest? Also ask if they used batching or any `mirror`/`fallback` settings.

maria: got this from their ingest logs (sanitized):
```
bulk_ingest start - model=rwd-embed-mini-int8 - batch_size=128
bulk_ingest chunk 1 - model=rwd-embed-mini-int8
bulk_ingest chunk 2 - model=rwd-embed-mini-int8
... error: vector schema mismatch - expected 256 got 512
```

maria: they confirmed they never requested `rwd-embed-mini-fused` or anything else.

rachel: ops-bot flagged a deploy on model-registry earlier today.

ops-bot: [notice] model-registry v2.9 deployed 2026-03-02T02:47:12Z - added auto-quantize pipeline and permissive aliasing for `-int8` suffix for canary models. Change-id: MR-2026-231

rachel: this matches. Hypothesis: the auto-quantize pipeline created a quantized variant from a different base checkpoint that projects to 512. The `-int8` alias was auto-assigned to that variant.

devon: mitigation plan (short term):
- pin `rwd-embed-mini-int8` alias back to the verified 256-dim quantized build used for customers.
- return a clear error header when clients try to ingest mismatched dims: e.g., `X-Expected-Embedding-Dim: 256` and `X-Embedding-Dim: 512` to make diagnosis obvious.

devon: medium term: add a model-registry guard that rejects alias creation if the candidate output dim differs from the family's baseline. Also add a CI step that verifies `embedding_dim` for every artifact pushed to registry.

maria: suggested customer messaging: offer immediate alias pin + 1 week of re-embed credits or assisted re-ingestion. They need to get past a tight launch window.

rachel: repro steps for us to validate locally:
1) call metadata endpoint for both aliases: `/v1/models/rwd-embed-mini-int8/metadata` and `/v1/models/rwd-embed-mini-fp16/metadata` and log `embedding_dim` and `checkpoint` fields.
2) run embeddings with both models and assert vector lengths. Try batch sizes 1 and 128 to rule out batching edge-cases.
3) run `model-registry` lookup for alias history (`/internal/model-registry/aliases?rwd-embed-mini-int8`) to see when mapping changed.

rachel: example metadata curl:
```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/rwd-embed-mini-int8/metadata
# expect json e.g. {"model":"rwd-embed-mini-int8","checkpoint":"embed-mini-v2","embedding_dim":256}
```
devon: note about precision: extreme quantization (int8 with aggressive per-channel scales) can hurt embedding quality (cosine similarity drift, higher retrieval false positives) but it should not change the vector length. If customers perceive quality drop, that's expected for some vectors but separate from length mismatch.

maria: customer also asked if batching could split or concat vectors — short answer: no, batching is independent. The only ways length changes are: different model variant, appended pooling outputs, or a serialization bug on our side.

rachel: I've started a short incident page and added owners: model-registry (owner: @devon) and runtime (owner: @rachel). Action items we've agreed on: 
- [ ] Pin alias to verified artifact and confirm with a smoke ingest by 20:30 UTC.
- [ ] Add `X-Embedding-Dim` response header in next quick patch and include it in SDKs.
- [ ] Audit all `-int8` aliases created in last 30 days for dimension mismatches and notify affected customers.
- [ ] Offer immediate assisted re-embed credits to the reporting customer.

devon: I'll do the alias pin now and post confirmation. Also starting the alias audit job.

maria: customer is online in the support channel; offering a pinned alias + walk-through would defuse this. I'll coordinate the communication and CC @devon once you've pinned.

rachel: one more note for eng: add a server-side validation that compares declared `embedding_dim` in model artifact to a family baseline on alias creation. Reject or flag for manual review if mismatch.

maria: thanks all. I'll update the customer and close the loop once the pin + smoke test succeed. :white_check_mark:
